title: Houda Angle
description: A transition angling drill where two attackers retrieve and advance the puck while three defenders recover through the middle, protect good ice, angle outside, and look to create a turnover that can immediately become offense.
coaching_points: Protect the middle before closing on the puck carrier.
Use forward skating and stick-on-puck pressure to steer play outside.
The second defender tracks support while the third reads whether to support defensively or transition.
Attackers use movement, give-and-go options, and creativity instead of simply dumping the puck.

title: 3 on 2 Dot Jumper
description: A 3-on-2 small-area game where each team begins with one player locked on a faceoff dot. A completed pass to that player activates them, creating the temporary numerical advantage.
coaching_points: Compete hard for initial possession.
Move without the puck and communicate to create the activation pass.
Protect possession once the extra player joins.
Follow shots and stay engaged around the net.

title: 3 on 2 with D Activation
description: A high-tempo rush drill where two forwards use a defenseman as a transition option, then attack back up ice as a 3-on-2 with that defenseman activated into the rush.
coaching_points: The activated defenseman joins quickly and fills useful ice.
Forwards support the puck without getting ahead of the play.
Defenders gap early and match the rush speed.
Attack with three lanes and make decisions off the defenders.

title: NZ Regroup
description: A neutral-zone regroup progression where three forwards work through multiple exchanges with defensemen, fill new lanes, then attack as a 3-on-2. The weak-side defenseman can also join to create a 4-on-2 variation.
coaching_points: Forwards swing through different lanes and remain available for the puck.
Keep sticks on the ice and face the puck during the regroup.
Defense moves the puck cleanly and keeps the rush outside.
Add a tracker or weak-side activation for progression.

title: 3 Regroup 3 vs. 2 Drill
description: A timing and passing progression where three forwards complete three neutral-zone regroups with two defense pairs before finishing by attacking one pair in a 3-on-2.
coaching_points: Forwards manage timing so they do not get ahead of the puck.
Communicate and fill open lanes on every regroup.
Defense keeps the head up and scans before moving the puck.
Finish the sequence with pace rather than treating the regroups as isolated passes.

title: Gretzky 3 vs 2 Behind the Net
description: A 3-on-2 game played below the tops of the circles where the offensive team must always keep one player below the goal line. Players rotate through the Gretzky spot to create switches and force defensive communication.
coaching_points: Offensive players rotate and switch behind the net to create confusion.
Keep one offensive player below the goal line at all times.
Defenders communicate through switches and protect dangerous space.
Use the net and goal line to change the point of attack.

title: Sabre Half-line Keep Away
description: A half-ice keep-away game split by an imaginary line. Each team can use all three players on its offensive side, but only two may cross to defend, creating a constant 3-on-2 possession challenge.
coaching_points: Offense keeps eyes up, moves feet, and creates support lanes.
Defense competes aggressively with stick-on-puck pressure.
Maintain one player on the offensive side to preserve the numerical advantage.
Transition the puck back across the line quickly after a turnover.

title: 3 v 3 with 3 Ways to Score
description: A 3-on-3 game with three scoring methods: complete a pass through two defenders, complete a one-touch pass, or score a goal. The format rewards quick reads and purposeful puck movement.
coaching_points: Offense scans for all three scoring options instead of forcing the net.
Move after passing to open the next lane.
Defenders keep sticks down and angle attackers outside.
Use the scoring rules to reinforce the practice concept being taught.

title: Regroup Game
description: A cross-ice 3-on-3 game where possession must be regrouped behind the team's own goal before attacking, forcing players to support underneath the puck and organize a new attack.
coaching_points: Support the puck carrier by becoming clear outlets.
Keep sticks on the ice as passing targets.
Defenders angle with active sticks and communicate coverage.
Use the regroup to attack with structure rather than simply throwing the puck forward.

title: Puck Race to 1 v 1
description: Two players race from the goal line to a loose puck on the dot. The winner becomes the puck protector while the other player defends, creating a competitive race that flows directly into a 1-on-1 possession battle.
coaching_points: Win body position before arriving at the puck.
The puck winner protects possession and keeps moving.
The defender uses body position and checking habits instead of reaching.
Use the race result to create immediate competitive pressure in the 1-on-1.
